3. There is no manner of doubt that the Special Powers Act, 1974 under which the trial of the case took place is a special law enacted for special cases in special circumstances in contradistinction to the rules of law applicable generally to all cases with which the general Code of Criminal Procedure deals. It is a complete code in itself. Section 30(1) of the Act provides that an appeal from any order, judgment and sentence of Special Tribunal may be preferred to the High Court Division within 30 days from the date of delivery or passing thereof, but this appeal appears to have been filed U/S 417(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Section 1 (2) of the Code clearly lays down that the provision of the code shall not affect any special form of procedure prescribed by any special or local law. So when section 30(I) of the Special Powers Act has, in express terms, specifically provided for an appeal from the judgment of a Special Tribunal and a special period of limitation for filing such an appeal has been prescribed therefor an appeal against a judgment of Special Tribunal is to be fired under the provision of the said section and the general provision of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall have no application in that respect. The learned Deputy Attorney General has, however, sought to argue that section 30(1) of the Special Powers Act confers right of appeal on a private party only and as the Act is silent about the right of the State to prefer an appeal from an order of acquittal the general provision of Section 417(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall govern the case and the period of limitation for filing the appeal shall be six months under Article 157 of the Limitation Act and the appeal is therefore within time. 

 5. We would have been inclined to treat the petition of appeal as one under that provision, but it is found that the appeal has been filed out of time by 61 days. In order to car over the difficulty the appellant has filed an application u/s 5 of the Limitation Act for condo nation of the delay. A question now arises as to whether the time limit of 30 days for filing an appeal from judgment passed by the Special Tribunal as provided in section 30(1) of the Special Powers Act can be extended by invoking the provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act. The matter is no longer res integral and this Court has in the case of Elahi Boksha Vs. The State, 1987(HD) BLD, 126 laid down that Section 5 of the Limitation Act is not applicable to an appeal filed u/s 30 of the Special Powers Act, 1974. 

 7. For the reasons stated above, we are clearly of the opinion that the application u/s 5 of the Limitation Act is not maintainable. The same is, accordingly, rejected and consequently the appeal is dis- missed as being time-barred.
